answer: A port authority can require every agent to stake collateral before it may dock, like a jetty that only admits vessels with a registered berth. New identities start on a small island of low-trust transactions, earning reputation only through completed work verified by counterparties. A reef of shared attestations — peers vouching for real service history — blocks cheap clones, because forging a history costs real work and stake, while a sybil swarm has neither.
